notes:
1. Reserve Bank of India — Central Bank

  • The Reserve Bank of India is India's central bank.
  • It occupies the central position in India's monetary and financial system.
  • It performs monetary, currency, banking, foreign-exchange, payment-system and financial-stability functions.
📌 Must-Memorise

India's Central Bank → RBI

2. Hilton Young Commission — 1926

  • The Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance recommended establishment of a central bank for India.
  • It is commonly known as the Hilton Young Commission.
  • The recommendation was made in 1926.
📌 Must-Memorise

Hilton Young Commission → Recommended RBI

3. RBI Act — 1934

  • The Reserve Bank of India Act was enacted in 1934.
  • It provided the statutory basis for establishment of RBI.
  • RBI therefore derives its basic legal authority from the RBI Act, 1934.
📌 Must-Memorise

RBI Act → 1934

RBI → Statutory Institution

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

RBI → Statutory

Planning Commission / NITI Aayog → Non-Statutory

4. RBI Commenced Operations — 1 April 1935

  • RBI began operations on 1 April 1935.
  • The Act was enacted in 1934, while the institution began functioning in 1935.
📌 Must-Memorise

RBI Started → 1 April 1935

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

RBI Act → 1934

RBI Operations → 1935

5. RBI Central Office — Kolkata to Mumbai

  • RBI's Central Office was initially located in Kolkata.
  • It was permanently shifted to Mumbai in 1937.
  • Mumbai became the principal location for major RBI policy formulation.
📌 Must-Memorise

Initial Office → Kolkata

1937 → Mumbai

6. RBI — Functions Taken Over at Establishment

When RBI began operations, it took over:

  • Important currency-related functions from the Government.
  • Management of Government accounts from the Imperial Bank of India.
  • Management of Government public debt from the Imperial Bank of India.
📌 Must-Memorise

Imperial Bank → Government Accounts + Public Debt → RBI

7. RBI — Original Ownership and Nationalisation

  • RBI was originally established as a shareholders' bank.
  • It was not fully Government-owned when it began operations in 1935.
  • RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949.
  • After nationalisation, it became fully owned by the Government of India.
📌 Must-Memorise

RBI Nationalisation → 1 January 1949

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

RBI in 1935 ≠ Fully Government-Owned

8. First RBI Governor — Sir Osborne Smith

  • Sir Osborne Smith was the first Governor of RBI.
  • He assumed office when RBI commenced operations in 1935.
📌 Must-Memorise

First RBI Governor → Sir Osborne Smith

9. First Indian RBI Governor — C. D. Deshmukh

  • C. D. Deshmukh was the first Indian Governor of RBI.
  • He became Governor in 1943.
  • He was serving as Governor when RBI was nationalised.
📌 Must-Memorise

First Indian RBI Governor → C. D. Deshmukh

10. RBI and Pakistan — Transitional Role

  • Around Independence and Partition, RBI temporarily performed central-banking functions for Pakistan.
  • This continued until the State Bank of Pakistan began functioning.

11. RBI Historical Chronology

  • 1926 → Hilton Young Commission recommendation.
  • 1934 → RBI Act.
  • 1 April 1935 → RBI began operations.
  • 1937 → Central Office shifted to Mumbai.
  • 1 January 1949 → RBI nationalised.
📌 Must-Memorise

1926 → 1934 → 1935 → 1937 → 1949

12. RBI — Core Statutory Objectives

  • RBI regulates the issue of banknotes.
  • It maintains reserves with a view to securing monetary stability.
  • It operates India's currency and credit system in the interests of the country.
  • The modern monetary framework emphasises price stability while keeping economic growth in mind.
📌 Must-Memorise

RBI Monetary Objective → Price Stability + Growth in Mind

13. RBI — Major Central-Banking Functions

RBI performs functions relating to:

  • Monetary policy.
  • Currency management.
  • Banking regulation.
  • Banking supervision.
  • Government banking.
  • Bankers' bank functions.
  • Foreign exchange.
  • Payment systems.
  • Financial stability.
  • Financial development.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

RBI ≠ Ordinary Retail Commercial Bank

14. Central Board of Directors

  • RBI's affairs are governed by the Central Board of Directors.
  • The Board is constituted under the RBI Act, 1934.
  • Its members are appointed or nominated by the Government of India according to the statutory framework.
📌 Must-Memorise

RBI Governing Body → Central Board of Directors

15. Governor and Deputy Governors

  • The Governor is RBI's chief executive authority.
  • The Governor plays a central role in policy formulation and implementation.
  • Deputy Governors are responsible for different functional areas of the Bank.
📌 Must-Memorise

RBI Chief Executive → Governor

16. RBI — Major Organisational Areas

RBI departments deal with areas such as:

  • Currency management.
  • Banking regulation.
  • Supervision.
  • Monetary policy.
  • Financial markets.
  • Foreign exchange.
  • Payment systems.
  • Financial inclusion.
  • Research.
  • Statistics.
  • Consumer protection.
  • Information technology.

17. RBI — India's Monetary Authority

  • One of RBI's most important responsibilities is formulation and implementation of monetary policy.
  • Monetary policy broadly concerns management of money, interest rates and liquidity to achieve macroeconomic objectives.
📌 Must-Memorise

India's Monetary Authority → RBI

18. Monetary Policy — Main Aim

  • RBI's monetary-policy framework seeks to maintain price stability while keeping economic growth in mind.
  • Monetary policy can influence liquidity, credit conditions, interest rates, inflation and economic activity.

19. RBI Act Amendment — 2016

  • RBI Act was amended in 2016 to provide statutory backing for the modern monetary-policy framework.
  • It also gave statutory backing to the Monetary Policy Committee framework.
📌 Must-Memorise

2016 → Statutory Backing for MPC Framework

20. Monetary Policy vs Fiscal Policy

  • Monetary policy is primarily associated with RBI.
  • Fiscal policy concerns Government taxation, expenditure, borrowing and budgetary policy.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Monetary Policy → RBI

Fiscal Policy → Government

21. Banknote Issuing and Currency Management

  • RBI performs the central function of issuing and managing banknotes.
  • It exchanges currency notes.
  • It removes unsuitable notes from circulation.
  • Currency management aims to maintain an adequate supply of good-quality notes and coins.
📌 Must-Memorise

Banknotes → RBI

22. Coins — Government of India and RBI Roles

  • Coins are minted by the Government of India.
  • RBI puts coins into circulation through the banking system.
📌 Must-Memorise

Coins → Minted by Government

Coins → Circulated through RBI

23. One-Rupee Note — Special Position

  • The one-rupee note is a liability of the Government of India.
  • It is not a liability of RBI.
  • It is legally treated in the same manner as the rupee coin.
📌 Must-Memorise

₹1 Note → Government of India Liability

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

₹1 Note ≠ RBI Liability

24. RBI Banknotes vs One-Rupee Note

  • Ordinary RBI banknotes → Liability of RBI.
  • One-rupee note → Liability of Government of India.

25. Minimum Reserve System — 1956

  • India follows the Minimum Reserve System for note issue.
  • It was introduced in 1956.
  • It replaced the earlier proportional reserve arrangement.
  • The system provided greater flexibility for meeting expanding currency requirements.
📌 Must-Memorise

Minimum Reserve System → 1956

26. RBI — Banker to Governments

  • RBI acts as banker to the Union Government.
  • It also acts as banker to State Governments.
  • It handles government banking transactions such as receipts, payments, accounts and remittances.
📌 Must-Memorise

RBI → Banker to Union + State Governments

27. Commercial Banks as RBI Agents

  • Commercial banks may act as RBI agents for conducting government banking business in different parts of the country.

28. RBI — Public Debt Management

  • Public debt refers to money borrowed by government to finance expenditure and fiscal requirements.
  • Public debt management has historically been an important RBI function.
  • RBI assists with issuance and servicing of government securities under the relevant institutional framework.
📌 Must-Memorise

RBI → Government Public Debt Management

29. Government Borrowing — Important Distinction

  • Government securities and Treasury instruments can be used for government borrowing.
  • The Government remains the actual borrower.
  • RBI acts as agent and debt manager in specified areas.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Government Borrowing ≠ RBI Borrowing on Its Own Behalf

30. RBI — Bankers' Bank

  • Commercial banks maintain banking relationships with RBI.
  • RBI maintains accounts of scheduled banks.
  • It facilitates inter-bank settlement.
  • Banks maintain prescribed reserves according to statutory and regulatory requirements.
📌 Must-Memorise

RBI → Bankers' Bank

31. Lender of Last Resort

  • RBI can provide liquidity support to the banking system during exceptional financial stress.
  • This function is known as lender of last resort.
  • Its purpose is to prevent temporary liquidity problems from developing into wider financial instability.
📌 Must-Memorise

RBI → Lender of Last Resort

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Lender of Last Resort ≠ Guaranteed Rescue of Every Bank

32. Liquidity vs Insolvency

  • A temporary liquidity shortage and fundamental insolvency are different financial problems.
  • Lender-of-last-resort support primarily addresses severe liquidity stress rather than automatically curing insolvency.

33. Cash Reserve Ratio — CRR

  • CRR stands for Cash Reserve Ratio.
  • It requires specified banks to maintain a prescribed proportion of relevant liabilities as cash balances with RBI.
  • CRR can influence banking-system liquidity and the funds available for lending.
📌 Must-Memorise

CRR → Cash with RBI

34. CRR — Historical and Policy Facts

  • RBI records show that scheduled banks were required to maintain cash balances with RBI from 1935.
  • The actual CRR percentage can change through monetary and regulatory decisions.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Do Not Memorise a Current CRR Rate as Permanently Fixed

35. RBI — Banking Regulator and Supervisor

  • RBI plays a major role in regulating India's banking system.
  • It also supervises important parts of the banking and financial system.
📌 Must-Memorise

Banking Regulation + Supervision → RBI

36. Banking Regulation Act — 1949

  • The Banking Regulation Act, 1949 provides an important statutory basis for banking regulation and supervision.
📌 Must-Memorise

Banking Regulation Act → 1949

37. RBI Regulation — Major Areas

RBI's regulatory framework can cover:

  • Capital requirements.
  • Liquidity requirements.
  • Lending practices.
  • Governance standards.
  • Risk management.
  • Operational standards.
  • Prudential requirements.

38. Banking Regulation — Main Objectives

Regulation and supervision seek to:

  • Protect depositors.
  • Maintain public confidence.
  • Improve financial soundness.
  • Reduce systemic risk.

39. RBI and NBFCs

  • RBI regulates and supervises relevant Non-Banking Financial Companies within the powers granted by law.
📌 Must-Memorise

Relevant NBFC Regulation / Supervision → RBI

40. Regulation vs Supervision

Regulation:

  • Establishes rules and standards.

Supervision:

  • Examines compliance and financial soundness.
📌 Must-Memorise

Regulation → Rules

Supervision → Compliance + Soundness

⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Regulation ≠ Supervision

41. Board for Financial Supervision — 1994

  • Board for Financial Supervision was established in 1994.
  • It was created as a committee of RBI's Central Board.
  • Its purpose was to strengthen supervision and monitoring of the financial system.
📌 Must-Memorise

Board for Financial Supervision → 1994

42. RBI — Foreign Exchange Role

  • RBI performs an important role in India's foreign-exchange framework.
  • It exercises regulatory powers under applicable foreign-exchange law.
  • It can authorise specified entities to undertake foreign-exchange transactions.

43. FEMA — 1999

  • FEMA stands for Foreign Exchange Management Act.
  • It was enacted in 1999.
  • RBI has important regulatory powers under FEMA.
📌 Must-Memorise

FEMA → 1999

44. Foreign-Exchange Reserves

  • RBI manages India's foreign-exchange reserves.
  • Reserves support external-payment capacity.
  • They can strengthen confidence.
  • They can help manage external shocks.
  • They support orderly functioning of foreign-exchange markets.
📌 Must-Memorise

Foreign-Exchange Reserves → RBI

45. RBI and Exchange Rate

  • RBI's foreign-exchange role does not mean India permanently follows a fixed exchange-rate system.
  • Exchange rates are influenced by market conditions.
  • RBI may intervene according to its policy objectives.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

Forex Management ≠ Permanent Fixed Exchange Rate

46. Payment and Settlement Systems Act — 2007

  • Payment and Settlement Systems Act was enacted in 2007.
  • Under this framework, RBI is the principal statutory authority for regulation and supervision of payment systems in India.
📌 Must-Memorise

PSS Act → 2007

Payment-System Regulator → RBI

47. Payment-System Objectives

RBI seeks to promote:

  • Safety.
  • Efficiency.
  • Reliability.
  • Integrity.

Modern payment infrastructure includes:

  • Electronic transfers.
  • Clearing systems.
  • Settlement systems.

48. Digital Payments — Growing RBI Role

  • Expansion of digital payments has increased the technological dimension of RBI's regulatory responsibilities.
  • Payment-system oversight has become increasingly important for financial stability and consumer confidence.

49. Digital Rupee — e₹

  • RBI has introduced a digital form of India's sovereign currency called the Digital Rupee or e₹.
  • It is issued by RBI.
  • It represents a digital form of sovereign currency.
📌 Must-Memorise

Digital Rupee → e₹ → RBI-Issued

50. Digital Rupee — Important Distinctions

  • e₹ is not an ordinary bank deposit.
  • e₹ is not a private cryptocurrency.
  • It is sovereign central-bank digital currency.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

e₹ ≠ Bank Deposit

e₹ ≠ Private Cryptocurrency

51. Financial Stability — Meaning

  • Financial stability means the financial system can continue performing essential functions even during economic or financial stress.

52. RBI — Financial Stability Role

RBI contributes through:

  • Regulation.
  • Supervision.
  • Liquidity management.
  • Risk monitoring.
  • Lender-of-last-resort functions.

53. Depositor and Consumer Protection

  • Depositor protection is an important objective of banking regulation.
  • RBI also performs functions related to consumer education and protection through dedicated institutional arrangements.

54. DICGC — Deposit Insurance

  • DICGC stands for Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation.
  • It provides deposit insurance in India.
  • It is a wholly owned subsidiary associated with RBI.
  • Deposit insurance protects eligible bank deposits subject to applicable legal limits and conditions.
📌 Must-Memorise

DICGC → Deposit Insurance

55. RBI vs DICGC

  • RBI → Central bank and regulator.
  • DICGC → Deposit insurance provider.
⚠️ TNPSC Trap

DICGC ≠ RBI

56. RBI — Developmental Role

  • RBI has historically performed developmental functions in addition to conventional central-banking functions.
  • It played an important role in agricultural finance.
  • It contributed to development of institutions related to agricultural credit, industrial finance and deposit insurance.
📌 Must-Memorise

RBI → Regulation + Development

57. Financial Inclusion — Meaning

  • Financial inclusion means expanding access to appropriate and affordable formal financial services.
📌 Must-Memorise

Financial Inclusion → Wider Access to Formal Finance

58. RBI — Financial Inclusion Role

Financial inclusion can improve access to:

  • Formal banking.
  • Safe savings.
  • Payment services.
  • Remittances.
  • Formal credit.
  • It can reduce excessive dependence on informal financial arrangements.

59. RBI Act — 1934

  • RBI Act provides the statutory basis for the Reserve Bank itself.
  • It also provides important authority relating to currency and monetary functions.

60. Banking Regulation Act — 1949

  • Banking Regulation Act provides important powers relating to banking regulation and supervision.

61. FEMA — 1999

  • FEMA provides the modern statutory framework for foreign-exchange management.

62. Payment and Settlement Systems Act — 2007

  • PSS Act provides the statutory framework for RBI regulation and supervision of payment systems.

63. Major RBI Laws — Memory Chain

  • RBI Act → 1934.
  • Banking Regulation Act → 1949.
  • FEMA → 1999.
  • PSS Act → 2007.
📌 Must-Memorise

1934 → 1949 → 1999 → 2007

64. RBI — Evolution of Role

Early post-Independence period:

  • Strong developmental role.
  • Agricultural credit.
  • Institutional finance.
  • Support for planned development.

Post-liberalisation:

  • Greater emphasis on core central-banking functions.

Modern role:

  • Monetary policy.
  • Banking regulation.
  • Supervision.
  • Financial markets.
  • Payment systems.
  • Financial stability.
  • Digital finance.

65. RBI — Core Institutional Identity

RBI =

Central Bank

  • Statutory Institution
  • Monetary Authority
  • Currency Manager
  • Government Banker
  • Bankers' Bank
  • Regulator
  • Forex Manager
  • Payment-System Regulator
📌 Must-Memorise

This is the core RBI identity chain.

66. Historical Memory Chain

  • Hilton Young Commission → 1926.
  • RBI Act → 1934.
  • RBI began → 1 April 1935.
  • Mumbai Central Office → 1937.
  • Nationalisation → 1 January 1949.

67. Governor Memory Chain

  • First Governor → Sir Osborne Smith.
  • First Indian Governor → C. D. Deshmukh.

68. Currency Memory Chain

  • Banknotes → RBI.
  • Coins → Government of India.
  • Coin circulation → RBI.
  • ₹1 note → Government of India liability.
  • Minimum Reserve System → 1956.

69. Government Banking Memory Chain

  • Banker to Union Government.
  • Banker to State Governments.
  • Government accounts.
  • Government receipts and payments.
  • Public debt management.
  • Government securities.

70. Banking-System Memory Chain

  • Bankers' Bank.
  • Scheduled-bank accounts.
  • Inter-bank settlement.
  • CRR.
  • Lender of Last Resort.
  • Regulation.
  • Supervision.

71. Foreign Exchange and Payments Memory Chain

  • FEMA → 1999.
  • Forex regulation → RBI.
  • Forex reserves → RBI.
  • PSS Act → 2007.
  • Payment-system regulator → RBI.
  • Digital Rupee → RBI.

72. TNPSC Traps

  • Hilton Young Commission recommended establishment of RBI.
  • RBI Act → 1934.
  • RBI operations began → 1 April 1935.
  • RBI Act year and commencement year are different.
  • Initial Central Office → Kolkata.
  • Central Office shifted to Mumbai → 1937.
  • RBI was originally a shareholders' bank.
  • RBI nationalised → 1 January 1949.
  • First Governor → Sir Osborne Smith.
  • First Indian Governor → C. D. Deshmukh.
  • RBI is statutory.
  • RBI is not an ordinary commercial bank.
  • RBI affairs are governed by Central Board of Directors.
  • Governor is chief executive authority.
  • Monetary policy is associated with RBI.
  • Fiscal policy is associated with Government.
  • RBI Act amended in 2016 for modern MPC framework.
  • RBI manages banknotes.
  • Coins are minted by Government of India.
  • RBI circulates coins.
  • ₹1 note is Government of India liability.
  • Minimum Reserve System → 1956.
  • RBI acts as banker to Union and State Governments.
  • RBI performs important public-debt-management functions.
  • Government remains the actual borrower.
  • RBI is bankers' bank.
  • RBI is lender of last resort.
  • Lender of last resort does not guarantee rescue of every institution.
  • CRR means cash balances with RBI.
  • Banking Regulation Act → 1949.
  • Regulation and supervision are different.
  • Board for Financial Supervision → 1994.
  • FEMA → 1999.
  • RBI manages foreign-exchange reserves.
  • Forex management does not imply permanent fixed exchange rate.
  • PSS Act → 2007.
  • RBI regulates payment systems.
  • Digital Rupee is issued by RBI.
  • e₹ is not a private cryptocurrency.
  • e₹ is not an ordinary bank deposit.
  • DICGC provides deposit insurance.
  • DICGC and RBI are separate institutions.
  • RBI has developmental as well as regulatory functions.
  • Financial inclusion is an important RBI responsibility.
  • Current CRR and policy rates can change and should not be treated as permanent facts.

73. Ultra-Short Memory Chain

  • Hilton Young → RBI.
  • Act → 1934.
  • Started → 1 April 1935.
  • Initial Office → Kolkata.
  • Mumbai → 1937.
  • Nationalised → 1 January 1949.
  • First Governor → Osborne Smith.
  • First Indian Governor → C. D. Deshmukh.
  • Central Bank → RBI.
  • Monetary Authority → RBI.
  • Banknotes → RBI.
  • Coins → Government.
  • ₹1 Note → Government Liability.
  • Minimum Reserve → 1956.
  • Government Banker → RBI.
  • Bankers' Bank → RBI.
  • Last Resort → RBI.
  • CRR → Cash with RBI.
  • Banking Regulation Act → 1949.
  • BFS → 1994.
  • FEMA → 1999.
  • Forex Reserves → RBI.
  • PSS Act → 2007.
  • Payment Regulator → RBI.
  • Digital Rupee → RBI.
  • Deposit Insurance → DICGC.

  • Recommendation year? → 1926.
  • RBI Act year? → 1934.
  • RBI commenced operations? → 1 April 1935.
  • Initial Central Office? → Kolkata.

  • Was RBI originally Government-owned? → No.
  • RBI nationalised? → 1 January 1949.
  • First RBI Governor? → Sir Osborne Smith.
  • First Indian RBI Governor? → C. D. Deshmukh.
  • RBI statutory or non-statutory? → Statutory.
  • Legal basis? → RBI Act, 1934.
  • Governing body? → Central Board of Directors.
  • Chief executive authority? → Governor.
  • India's monetary authority? → RBI.
  • Main monetary-policy objective? → Price stability while keeping growth in mind.
  • RBI Act amended for MPC framework? → 2016.
  • Who issues banknotes? → RBI.
  • Who mints coins? → Government of India.
  • Who puts coins into circulation? → RBI.
  • ₹1 note liability? → Government of India.
  • Minimum Reserve System introduced? → 1956.
  • RBI banker to whom? → Union and State Governments.
  • RBI public-debt role? → Government debt management and agency functions.
  • Bankers' bank? → RBI.
  • Lender of last resort? → RBI.
  • CRR full form? → Cash Reserve Ratio.
  • CRR maintained where? → With RBI.
  • Banking Regulation Act? → 1949.
  • Regulation means? → Setting rules.
  • Supervision means? → Checking compliance and financial soundness.
  • Board for Financial Supervision? → 1994.
  • FEMA? → 1999.
  • Forex reserve manager? → RBI.
  • Permanent fixed exchange rate because RBI manages forex? → No.
  • PSS Act? → 2007.
  • Payment-system regulator? → RBI.
  • Digital Rupee issuer? → RBI.
  • Digital Rupee name/symbol? → e₹.
  • e₹ private cryptocurrency? → No.
  • e₹ ordinary bank deposit? → No.
  • Deposit insurance provided by? → DICGC.
  • DICGC associated with? → RBI.
  • Does RBI perform developmental functions? → Yes.
  • Financial inclusion means? → Wider access to appropriate and affordable formal financial services.
